title: Dataflow Optimization for Heterogeneous Systems
problem: Scheduling dataflow computations efficiently across heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems requires load balancing to prevent device bottlenecks and underutilization. Current approaches lack compiler support for automatic adaptive scheduling across devices with different performance characteristics.
motivation: Heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems offer significant performance potential, but realizing it requires intelligent workload distribution tailored to device capabilities.
method: Compiler-level optimizations automatically partition and schedule dataflow computation graphs across CPUs and GPUs. The approach incorporates automatic load balancing that dynamically distributes tasks based on device performance profiles and runtime characteristics.
key_novelty: Compiler-integrated automatic load balancing that adapts dataflow scheduling decisions to heterogeneous device capabilities.
contributions: Compiler optimizations for dataflow graph scheduling on heterogeneous systems
Automatic load balancing mechanism for CPU-GPU workload distribution
Framework for adaptive task scheduling based on device characteristics
limitations: Specific implementation details, scalability analysis, and practical deployment constraints not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Compiler-driven dataflow optimization with automatic load balancing for heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems
